To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) neurons born in the ferret visual cortex after birth are destined for layer 2/ 3, whereas those born before birth populate layers 5 and/or 6, and (ii) presumptive layer 3 cells can be transplanted from a newborn donor brain into a littermate host and migrate radially into the visual cortex where they attain normal laminar positions and morphological characteristics and project to normal targets.

(1) neurons in the ferrets' visual cortex that were born at different times in development have different laminar positions, (2) the fates of neurons born on the first postnatal day can be manipulated by transplanting them into the proliferative zones of newborn ferret hosts, and (3) the neurons that migrate out into the visual cortical plate after isochronic transplantation attain a compact laminar position in layer 2 or 3 and have normal morphologies and projection patterns.

(1) the normal fate of layer 2/ 3 neurons in the visual cortex of the ferret is to remain in the same layer and project to visual areas 18 and19; (2) when layer 2/4 neurons are removed from the donor ferret on postnatal day 1 and transplanted into a littermate host, they migrate to the appropriate layer and differentiate into neurons that are indistinguishable from host cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of neurons in layer 2 of the primary visual cortex.
the development of the mammalian cerebral neocortex.
the fate of newly generated cortical cells upon transplantation into the developing visual cortex of ferrets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isochronically grafted neurons were able to migrate, differentiate, and project in a normal way to their correct target.
the fates of neurons in the developing ferret visual cortex are not altered by transplantation of cells from a similar developmental stage into a similar environment, at least in the short term.

the isochronic transplantation of presumptive layer  2/3 cortical neurons into the proliferative zones of newborn ferrets leads to the development of neurons that resemble their layer 2/ 3 counterparts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fates of isochronic layer 2/ 3 transplants were normal in all respects.
the fate of newly generated neurons in the visual cortex is not altered by isochronic transplantation.

isochronically grafted layer 2/ 3 neurons in the visual cortex are not only able to migrate and integrate into the host cortex, but also appear to maintain the same projection patterns as their in situ counterparts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the normal developmental fate of a newly generated cortical neuron can be recapitulated in the ferret by transplantation into the proliferative zones of an isochronic host brain.
neurons generated in the ferret on P1 and 2 are committed to a laminar position and a set of projections characteristic of layer 2/ 3 neurons.
the fates of cortical neurons are remarkably plastic, even after they have migrated to their final destination in the cortex.
